answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with staking-weighted attestation. Each identity locks a stake that decays like an ember: a fixed portion burns every epoch, and restoring it requires verified work for established peers. Trust accrues per stake-year, not per identity, so a whisper network of fake accounts splitting one attacker's funds gains no more voting weight than a single account. The burn cost is identical whether spread thin or kept together. Honest relic accounts earn slow reputation multipliers, making old identities costly to abandon and cheap ones worthless to multiply.
